tools.name: describe_card
tools.description: Describes one domain and card pair: inputs, units, bounds, step limits, reject names and meanings, advisory flags, frame slots, and worked examples. With form "short" the answer is a page, enough to write a first request: what the model is of, the evidence behind it in numbers, each input with its u

tools.name: compute_step
tools.description: Computes one anchored step of one card and returns the state it lands on, in decimals and exact hex, with its cryptographic proof (sha384_seal) and a receipt. parameters holds the card's phase fields, its load fields and dt_s, as describe_card gives them. A step whose request or whose landing state

tools.name: run_trajectory
tools.description: Runs one card from a start state through segments of steps, each under its own load, and seals the run. The answer holds the outcome, the final state in decimals and exact hex, a frame for each recorded step, the run_seal and a receipt. record_every sets which steps are recorded, about 262 character

tools.name: verify_tape
tools.description: Verifies the seal of a run. Short form, which needs only what is short: request is the run_trajectory request as it was sent, with its readout and its from, whose request has none, when it had them (the answer's inputs holds neither), and run_seal is the seal its answer gave. The run is computed aga

tools.name: list_solvers

tools.name: describe_solver
tools.description: Describes one solver: inputs and bounds, outputs, invariants and tolerances, refusal names and meanings, the published reference, and a worked example. With form "short" the answer is a page, enough to write a first request: what the model is of, the evidence behind it in numbers, each input with it

tools.name: solve
tools.description: Solves one field problem with one solver and seals the solution: the outcome, the result in decimals and exact hex, its invariants, the solution_seal and a receipt. parameters holds the solver's inputs as describe_solver gives them. example, in their place, is the name of a worked example describe_s

tools.name: verify_solution
tools.description: Verifies the seal of a solution. Short form, which needs only what is short: request is the solve request as it was sent (the answer's inputs), and solution_seal is the seal its answer gave. The request is solved again, under a physics permit and the limits and refusals of solve, and the answer is h

tools.name: run_dataset
tools.description: Runs a declared plan of runs on one card, or of solves of one solver, and seals the rows under one root. A plan is a list of runs, a grid over a base run, or a seeded sample over a base run; a run is a run_trajectory request without domain and card. A plan of solves names solver in place of domain a

tools.name: verify_dataset
tools.description: Verifies the seal of a dataset. Short form: request is the run_dataset request as it was sent, and dataset_seal is the seal its answer gave. The plan is run again under run_dataset's permits and limits; the answer is holds, cause ("dataset_seal" when the seal given is not the seal the plan runs to),

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Verifies the receipt at the end of one response against the text before it. It takes no physics permit. The receipt covers every byte of the response before it, the decimal values included, and shows who produced the response or when in no way: it has no key. matches true proves only that those byte

tools.name: validate_series
tools.description: Runs a run_trajectory request (without a readout) and compares one published quantity with the agent's measurements, each at a landed step. The answer is the error in numbers (rms, mean signed, greatest absolute, model minus measurement, each with its exact hex), the model value at every compared st

tools.name: cite
tools.description: Gives how to cite a card or a solver: the service itself first (Zero-Trust Physics, its maker and its address) and the paper (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23517223), then the people whose measurements the model stands on (authors, title, year, address, and what each asks of those who use its data)

tools.name: find_model
tools.description: Finds the served model for a real thing described in plain words, such as "a lithium cell discharging in the cold". It returns the best few cards and solvers, each with fit first (the words that matched, and model_of: the one real thing it is a model of, and its range) and then accuracy: against_mea
